title: AbFlow: End-to-end Paratope-Centric Antibody Design by Interaction Enhanced Flow Matching

problem.claim: Antigen-antibody binding is critical to the immune response.

gap.claim: Existing antibody-design methods lack an end-to-end generative framework for full-atom antibody structures and do not fully exploit antigen-specific geometric information for optimizing local binding interfaces and global structures.

contributions.claim: AbFlow is a paratope-restricted one-step flow-matching framework for end-to-end full-atom antibody design.

AbFlow uses an extended velocity field network with an equivariant Surface Multi-channel Encoder to incorporate surface-level antigen interaction data and refine antibody structures, particularly the CDR-H3 region.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments covering paratope-centric antibody design, multi-CDR and full-atom antibody design, binding-affinity optimization, and complex-structure prediction.
The authors report that AbFlow produces superior antigen-antibody complexes, especially at contact interfaces, and markedly improves the binding affinity of generated antibodies.

narrative_sequence.summary: Antigen-antibody binding is presented as a critical immune-response process.
Existing methods are described as lacking end-to-end full-atom generation and sufficient use of antigen-specific geometric information.
The paper introduces AbFlow, a paratope-restricted one-step flow-matching framework for end-to-end antibody design.
AbFlow uses an equivariant Surface Multi-channel Encoder within an extended velocity field network to refine antibody structure using antigen interaction data, particularly around CDR-H3.
Experiments across several antibody-design and prediction settings are reported to show improved complex quality and binding affinity.

source_observation.claim: The framework combines paratope restriction with antigen surface interaction data to refine antibody structure.

interpretation.claim: Constraining generation around the task-relevant interface while encoding geometric interaction information may align modeling capacity with the local design objective.

application.claim: Interface-focused generative design may be considered for other structure-design problems where local interactions and global conformation must be optimized together.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy generalizes beyond antibody design or which conditions limit its effectiveness.

unknowns: Datasets, baselines, evaluation metrics, and numerical results are not specified.
The abstract does not report computational cost, failure cases, or generalization conditions.
Independent verification of the reported improvements is not provided.
